[MUQATIL:11:68/r1] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | The phrase means that the people of Thamud seemed never to have lived in this world.
[MUQATIL:11:68/r2] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | Thamud disbelieved in the oneness of their Lord, and the prayer that they be far away refers to their destruction.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأسماءالقبائلوالأحياءومايضافإلىالأبوالأم)#542/r13] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Thamud and Saba can denote either a tribe lineage or a living community; Sībawayh cites Qur'anic forms of both names as evidence for these uses.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكرأيتزيداوعمراكلمتهورأيتعبدms037اللهوزيدامررتبهولقيت#52/r1] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | prefers | When an accusative noun is followed by another coordinated noun, accusative is preferred if both are construed with the verb; Qur'anic examples include ثمودا, فريقا, and الظالمين. | mentions 76:31, 25:38, 25:39, 7:30
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكرأيتزيداوعمراكلمتهورأيتعبدms037اللهوزيدامررتبهولقيت#52/r2] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The same verb based accusative coordination works with كان and ليس, which behave like verbs in their government.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكرأيتزيداوعمراكلمتهورأيتعبدms037اللهوزيدامررتبهولقيت#52/r3] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Raising the second noun is also good when it begins an independent clause; it is more natural the closer that noun stands to the beginning.
[SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكرأيتزيداوعمراكلمتهورأيتعبدms037اللهوزيدامررتبهولقيت#52/r5] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | After ولكن or بل, the second noun follows the same accusative or permitted nominative patterns as a noun joined by ordinary conjunctions, since these particles govern nothing.
[FARRA:v2p20/r1] FARRA, d. 207 · الأسود بن يزيد | reports | Al-Aswad ibn Yazīd did not decline Thamūd anywhere in the Qurʾan, and Ḥamza followed this reading.
[FARRA:v2p20/r2] FARRA, d. 207 · الكسائي | reports | Some readers decline Thamūd in the accusative because it is written with alif; al-Kisāʾī follows that in accusative but generally leaves it indeclinable in nominative and genitive.
[FARRA:v2p20/r3] FARRA, d. 207 · الكسائي | reports | Al-Kisāʾī exceptionally declines the second occurrence لثمود because it is close to the first; he considered differing case on the repeated word awkward.
[FARRA:v2p20/r4] FARRA, d. 207 · جاء في التفسير | reports | The exegetical gloss is كفروا نعمة ربهم; Arabic permits كفرتك and كفرت بك, as well as several constructions with شكر.
[FARRA:v2p20/r5] FARRA, d. 207 · الكسائي | reports | Al-Kisāʾī heard Arabs say شكرت بالله, by analogy with كفرت بالله.
[AKHFASH:v1p384/r4] AKHFASH, d. 215 · author | prefers | Thamūd is declined when understood as the people or their ancestor; the non-declined reading treats it as a feminine tribal name, but Akhfash reads the declined form and allows declension generally for a masculine people or ancestor name.
[TAB-FULL:v12p465/r1] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | The cry struck those who wrongfully hamstrung God's she-camel and disbelieved; death left them motionless in their courtyards, as though they had never lived there. | mentions 11:67

[TAB-FULL:v12p465/r6] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | Thamud disbelieved in their Lord by denying His signs.

[MAWARDI-FULL:v2p480/r12] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · author | reports | Alternatively, it was as if they had never enjoyed its prosperity.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v2p480/r13] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · author | reports | One gloss is that Thamūd denied their Lord’s threat.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v2p480/r14] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · author | reports | Another gloss is that they disbelieved God’s command.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v2p480/r15] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · author | holds | The destruction annihilated Thamūd except Abū Ramḥān, who was in God’s sanctuary and was protected from the punishment.

[WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p464#2/r2] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · author | holds | The name Thamud is read either with declension or without: with declension when it names the masculine people, without it when it names the tribe.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p464#2/r3] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · أبو علي | reports | Since Thamud can name either the tribe or its people and neither reading has an advantage, both declension and indeclinability are sound, as with Yahud and Majus.

[WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p464#2/r5] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · الحديث | reports | The hadith wording تقسم يهود likewise treats Yahud as a tribal name.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p464#2/r6] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · الشاعر | reports | An anonymous poet uses Majus as a tribal name; if it referred only to people it would take declension.
[JISHUMI:v5p3525/r12] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | To dwell in a place means to remain there; dwellings are called maghani because people find sufficiency in them, while the root ghina denotes sufficiency.

[BIQAI-FULL:v3p550#2/r11] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | Alā is an alerting formula used for momentous matters, meant to keep a heedless listener from overlooking what follows.

item.text: The notes point to two main areas of disagreement: how the two occurrences of “Thamūd” are read, and whether “as though they had not lived there” emphasizes residence or former prosperity.
